spine: One agent is mid-job when you walk away from the desk — and the film follows that single job from your pocket: you read it, you interrupt it, you answer it out loud, you approve its diff, you see what it cost, all on a relay you own — and only at the very end does the camera pull back to show that fifteen more finished the same way while you weren't looking.
why: A feature montage asks the viewer to count. A followed job asks them to care what happens next, which is the only reason anyone watches forty silent seconds. Eight capabilities are not eight items here — they are the eight things that happen to one piece of work between you closing the laptop and it being done, so the viewer learns the product as a sequence of consequences rather than a menu. Crucially the film withholds "sixteen" until 31 seconds in: the narrative lens is right that quantity only reads as power when the viewer counted to one first. Start wide on sixteen panes and it is a list; pull back to sixteen after they have watched one pane succeed and it is a revelation about scale. And the outcome is not asserted anywhere — it is the last two shots, where the Inbox holds five rows that say "pi finished" and the viewer works out for themselves that they were somewhere else the whole time. Four of the eight capabilities are never captioned at all; they are carried by the product's own on-screen words (the ctrl/shift/esc/^C key row, the desk scrollback, "269.4M / $177", "Local plugin · UI only", "YOU RUN THE RELAY", "16 agents", "pi finished"). That is the structural answer to the list problem: half the film's claims are evidence, not copy.
openingSeconds: Frames 0-90, one continuous shot, no cut, no fade-up — the film is simply already running at f0, Linear-style. f0: ink ground #0a0a0c, and a single LIVE pane card lifted from dark/herd.mp4 fills 92% of frame height, cropped so its rounded corners sit just outside the left and right frame edges — the viewer is inside the product before they know what the product is. Mean frame luma 7%. vignette({amount:0.5,radius:0.62,feather:0.35}) and noise({amount:0.055,premultiply:true,seed:7}) are on from frame one, and the highlight cap (contrast+brightness so no pixel reaches 255) is already applied, so it reads as photographed rather than exported. A breathing push runs the whole shot, scale 1.000 to 1.038 over 156f via interpolate with Easing.bezier(0.33,0,0.67,1) and output:'perceptual-scale' — 1.3%/sec, deliberately below the threshold where a viewer can name it as a move. f18: a new line of real agent output lands in the pane. That is the first thing that changes, and it comes from the capture, not from us. f36: the card's footer resolves — "store-audit", a 10px blue #0A84FF working dot, "Working · Pi · /home/umer/pockit". That dot is the only saturated pixel in the frame and it is Hitchcock's clock: something is in flight. f54-72: two more lines arrive, the pane scrolls one line. f90: no cut has happened, no type has appeared, the subject has not changed. The film has committed to one image and held it, which every measured reference film does and no rejected version did.
endingFrame: f1186, held dead still for 26 frames with only one thing moving. Ink ground #0a0a0c, nothing else on it. The muxr display-matrix wordmark sits centred, assembled one cell-column at a time between f1104 and f1126 (the repo's existing genBrand.sh rasterisation, so the mark is the product's mark and not a redrawn one). Below it on the 8px baseline, one line of IBM Plex Mono, centre-aligned, typed out character by character from f1126 to f1160 so it grows outward from the middle: "Leave the desk. Not the work." A solid block cursor is still lit at the end of it, blinking on Math.floor(frame/12)%2 — frame-derived, no wall clock. Two micro lines in dim #8a8a90 faded in at f1168: "npm install -g --ignore-scripts @trymuxr/cli" and "trymuxr.com". No product on screen. No screenshot. No green. No motion but the cursor. 8 frames to black at f1192.

shots.what: f0-156. One unbroken shot, no cut in the first five seconds. A single LIVE pane card from dark/herd.mp4 at macro, filling 92% of frame height, real agent output arriving line by line. At f36 the footer resolves: store-audit, 10px blue working dot, 'Working · Pi · /home/umer/pockit'. From f108 the image is progressively swallowed — linearProgressiveBlur start [0,0.15] end [0,1] with endBlur ramping 0 to 40, and overall brightness falling 1.00 to 0.14 over 54f — the laptop closing, staged as light dying rather than an object moving. f162-180 sits at 4% luma, near black but never #000.
shots.camera: Locked, plus a breathing push scale 1.000 to 1.038 across the whole 156f. Easing.bezier(0.33,0,0.67,1), output:'perceptual-scale'. 1.3%/sec — invisible as a move, present as life.
shots.screenTreatment: Full bleed, no device, no bezel, no frame edge. The capture is cropped so its own corner radii fall outside frame, so the viewer is inside the screen rather than looking at one.
shots.typeTreatment: Nothing until f108. Then 'YOU LEAVE' in IBM Plex Sans SemiBold micro (14px, tracking 1.6, uppercase, dim #8a8a90), centred, entering opacity 0 to 1 over 14f with a 16px upward translate on Easing.bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1). Holds to f150 (42f, exactly the two-word minimum). Exits opacity-only over 9f, no translate. The image leads by 18 frames; type never arrives first.
shots.transitionIn: None — the film opens already running at full exposure. No fade-up, no logo, no title card.
shots.feature: Real terminal panes with live scrollback

shots.what: f156-270. The establish, and the only shot in the film containing a device. A whole handset, straight-on, dead centre, occupying 84% of frame height on ink with real negative space either side. On its screen: the same pane card from shot 1, still streaming, nothing lost. Two Lightformer strips sweep 45° across the glass between f186 and f240 — the reflection travels, the phone does not.
shots.camera: Absolutely locked. Zero rotation, zero tilt, zero dolly, camera dead straight-on. Apple's own partner guideline: establish the entire device once, never animate/flip/spin it. All apparent motion is the specular sweep and the pixels.
shots.screenTreatment: R3F 3D device: extrudeGeometry over a THREE.Shape rounded rect in meshPhysicalMaterial (metalness 0.9, roughness 0.28, clearcoat 1, envMapIntensity 1.2); the screen is a separate shapeGeometry plane proud of the body with meshBasicMaterial toneMapped={false} so the UI ignores scene lighting; ContactShadows frames={1} beneath plus a wide ambient shadow at 6% opacity. Screen fed by dark/herd.mp4 as a live CanvasTexture.
shots.typeTreatment: Beside the device, never on it — columns 1-4, bottom margin. f186: kicker '01 / CONTINUITY' mono micro dim, hairline rule (2px, ground.rule), then display 'The same pane. In your pocket.' at Bricolage Bold 84/88/-2.6. Word stagger 3f. Holds to f262, exits opacity over 9f.
shots.transitionIn: Hard cut, and a scale match cut: the pane card that filled shot 1's frame is the same card now inside the phone's screen at 0.38 scale, same aspect, same position on the horizontal centre. The eye carries the object across the cut.
shots.feature: Continuity — the actual pane, not a mirror

shots.what: f270-348. Punch-in on the cut to full bleed, no device. dark/terminal.mp4 cropped to the bottom 620px of the capture: the terminal key row (1 · folder · branch · ctrl · shift · esc · tab · ^C) and the composer. The composer fills with real typed text, the send arrow presses, then ^C presses and the pane interrupts. Every press goes darker and in: scale 0.97, brightness 0.88, 3f in / 5f out. A 4-frame luminance flash at 1.18 on the key that acted — the silent film's replacement for a sound effect.
shots.camera: Completely locked. No move of any kind. The content is moving, so the camera is not — this is the rule that keeps punch-ins from reading as Ken Burns.
shots.screenTreatment: Full bleed, extreme crop, no device edge visible. Sits at roughly 1:1 against the source so the mono glyphs are genuinely sharp.
shots.typeTreatment: None. The product's own key caps are the typography of this shot. Captioning 'you can type into it' over an image of a keyboard is the deck.
shots.transitionIn: Hard cut carrying a 2.4x scale jump. The magnitude comes from cutting between two scales, never from moving fast within one.
shots.feature: Type into it, interrupt it (^C) — real control

shots.what: f348-444. The voice orb at macro. dark/voice.mp4 cropped to rect [150,380,780,780] and scaled so the particle field fills 70% of frame height, sitting right of centre. The particles genuinely move — this is real product motion, not a drawn waveform. glow({radius:24,intensity:0.55,threshold:0.72}) applied to the orb layer alone so only the bright particles bloom. The word 'Listening' from the real capture sits under it at product scale.
shots.camera: Lateral drift only: 2.4% of frame width, linear, running the full 96f. Linear's continuous creep — never stops, never arrives.
shots.screenTreatment: Extracted fragment floating full-bleed on ink, cropped hard so no device and no status bar appear. The surrounding ground is the frame's own negative space, not a blurred duplicate.
shots.typeTreatment: Left half, bottom margin. f378: kicker '02 / VOICE' + hairline + display 'Say it. Don't type it.' Holds to f434 (56f for four words). The claim and the product's own 'Listening' label are both visible in the same frame — the copy is confirmed on screen rather than asserted over it.

shots.what: f444-522. The Kuleshov shot, and the cheapest shot in the film. Full-bleed desk terminal plate rendered in React from lib/desk.json — real scrollback from the same pane, at desk width, in IBM Plex Mono on ink. Lines type on one at a time, 3f stagger, caret leading the edge. In the lower-right 22% of frame the handset from shot 2 sits small, its orb still lit. Two shots, no explanation: you spoke there, the machine wrote here. Causation is inferred, never captioned. Note the plate's text and the phone capture's text are literally the same POLISH-REPORT scrollback — the match is real, not staged.
shots.camera: Locked. The text arriving is the entire motion.
shots.screenTreatment: Rendered plate, not footage — the desk half is DOM/React; the phone is the 3D device layer reused at 0.22 scale with its own contact shadow.
shots.typeTreatment: None from us. The scrollback is the type, and it is the product's own words.
shots.transitionIn: Hard cut, position match: the orb sits frame-right in shot 4 and the phone carrying that orb sits lower-right in shot 5. Same screen region, different world behind it.
shots.feature: NONE — this is the pure graphic beat that makes 'action at a distance' legible

shots.what: f522-630. The ground inverts. Paper #f2f1ed. Full-bleed light/changes.mp4 cropped to the diff body: per-file tab rail (All / index.tsx / _layout.tsx), real dual gutter with -1/+1 and -71/+71 line numbers, red and green marks at native line height. Real scroll for the first 38 frames, then the frame settles.
shots.camera: Locked f522-576. Then one move and only one: a 22-frame push, scale 1.00 to 1.34, Easing.bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), landing on the gutter at f598 — the move arrives on the thing that is about to change. Locked again f598-630. Velocity-derived blur peaks at 4px mid-move.
shots.screenTreatment: Full bleed, no device, corner radii cropped out of frame. Highlight cap especially important here — a white paper UI that reaches 255 is the export tell.
shots.typeTreatment: f552: kicker '03 / REVIEW' + hairline + display 'Read it before you approve.' in ground.paper text #111113. Holds to f620 (68f for five words). Same grid position, same sizes as shots 2 and 4 — the type block does not move across the ground flip, which is what makes the flip read as deliberate.
shots.transitionIn: Hard cut on the inversion — no dissolve, no fade. Geometry holds across the cut (screen fills frame on both sides), only the ground flips ink to paper. This is the film's one structural surprise and it costs nothing to build.
shots.feature: Diff review with a real dual gutter

shots.what: f630-690. The hero lift, still on paper. The approve row detaches from the plane and translates 90px toward camera over 20f on spring({damping:200,mass:3}), with dropShadow({radius:18,offsetY:14,opacity:0.28}) beneath it. Critically, the rect it vacated on the parent is darkened to brightness 0.82 and blurred 6px — the element came out of somewhere. The parent plane racks out via radialProgressiveBlur with center on the lifted row, endBlur 0 to 14 over 16f. Then the row presses: scale 0.97, brightness 0.88, 3f/5f, and a 4-frame flash at 1.18. Approved.
shots.camera: Locked. The element moves in z; the camera does not.
shots.screenTreatment: UI lifted out of the screen into z-space — a real layer at z with its own shadow, the parent defocused behind it. Apple's own keynote grammar, the mode they forbid partners from using.
shots.typeTreatment: None. Shortest shot in the film (60f) and the only one under 2.2s — it is a punctuation mark, not a statement.
shots.feature: Approve from the phone — you stay in control

shots.what: f690-768. Back to ink, hard. Full-bleed dark/usage.mp4 cropped to the numbers: 269.4M / $177, 'Left 79%', '5-hour window · 3h 57m left · 1.6M tokens/min', claude-opus-5 268.4M, and the 7-day block 1.7B / $1461 with its bar chart. The bars grow from the capture. Every number is real and tabular.
shots.camera: Absolutely locked, no move at all, not even a breathing push. The numbers shot is the one shot that gets nothing — Apple does this and it reads as confidence.
shots.screenTreatment: Full bleed, tight crop so the digits are large enough to read at 1920x1080 without punching in.
shots.typeTreatment: One mono micro line only, bottom-left, f712 to f764 (52f): 'READ FROM YOUR OWN LOGS'. No display size, no kicker, no rule. Second register, deliberately — the four structural claims get display type, the two footnotes get micro. Four sizes is how a set stops looking designed.
shots.transitionIn: Hard cut, ground flips paper back to ink. Second and last inversion.
shots.feature: Token and dollar spend read from your own logs

shots.what: f768-846. dark/plugins.mp4 full bleed, cropped to the rows — each carrying 'Local plugin · UI only' in the product's own text. Rows stagger in 4f apart, each doing opacity + 14px translateY + blur 12 to 0 simultaneously, with the row boundaries found by scanning the capture's flat ground on the vertical axis (the same technique fragments.mjs already uses to find chip boundaries horizontally). At f804 the right 38% of frame becomes the authoring CLI panel rendered from lib/authoring.json, typing on: '$ muxr plugin create field-notes' then 'created ./field-notes (local.field-notes)'. The extension system and writing your own extension are one shot, not two.
shots.camera: Locked. The plugin rows carry a 1.8% lateral drift while the CLI panel stays still, so the two halves move at different rates — parallax between planes, which is what stops a split reading as a comparison table.
shots.screenTreatment: Full bleed left, rendered React panel right. Two surfaces, one stage.
shots.typeTreatment: One mono micro line, f792 to f842 (50f): 'NATIVE UI. NO WEBVIEWS.' The 'write your own' claim is made entirely by the CLI panel typing a real command. Nothing captions it.
shots.feature: Extensions as native UI through a bounded API, plus authoring your own

shots.what: f846-912. dark/connection.mp4 cropped to the 'YOU RUN THE RELAY' block — 'End-to-end encrypted', 'Pairing holds the credentials', 'Use your own network, Tailscale, or your own secure tunnel.' The crop must sit below the Relay row (see risks). A 10px green done dot from the Transport row is the only colour.
shots.camera: Locked plus a breathing push 1.00 to 1.04 across 66f, Easing.bezier(0.33,0,0.67,1), perceptual-scale.
shots.screenTreatment: Full bleed, tight crop on the card, its rounded rect fully visible — this shape is the match-cut anchor for the next shot.
shots.typeTreatment: f862: kicker '04 / SELF-HOSTED' + hairline + display 'Your relay. Your rules.' Holds to f906 (44f). Fourth and final display line in the film.

shots.what: f912-1008. The payoff, and the longest shot since the open. Opens on ONE session row from dark/herd.mp4 at 2.4x — close, half-legible, its status dot the only anchor. Then one continuous pull-back: scale 2.4 to 0.62 over 84 frames. As the camera retreats the rest of the Spaces list resolves around it, and at f990 the header line becomes legible in the product's own type: 'pockit  /home/umer/pockit   16 agents'. Sixteen is not a graphic we drew — it is printed on the real screen. Then dead locked f990-1008.
shots.camera: One move, 3.9x total change, Easing.bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) with output:'perceptual-scale' so it decelerates hard into the wide. Velocity-derived blur peaks ~5px around f930 with chromaticAberration({amount:2}) at the same peak. Then locked for the final 18 frames — the brake.
shots.screenTreatment: Full bleed. Start the first 12 frames from the sharp raw/dark/herd.png still and crossfade to the mp4 at f924, so the 2.4x enlargement never shows interpolation.
shots.typeTreatment: ZERO. No kicker, no rule, no headline, nothing. The single most important discipline in the film: the product prints '16 agents' itself and repeating it in Bricolage Bold turns a revelation into a caption.
shots.transitionIn: Hard cut, scale match: the relay card's rounded rect in shot 10 and the session row's rounded rect here share corner radius and screen position. Same container, different contents — Arc's fixed-container trick, executed as a cut.
shots.feature: Sixteen agents at once — the scale claim

shots.what: f1008-1092. dark/inbox.mp4 full bleed: '/HOME/UMER/POCKIT' and beneath it leak-scan · pi finished, site-film · pi finished, suite-check · pi finished, pr93opus · pi finished, warp · pi finished. Rows arrive staggered 5f, each with opacity + 12px translateY + blur 10 to 0. Five green #30D158 dots at 10px — the entire green budget of the film, spent here, at dot size, on the word 'finished'. Then f1068-1092 is a FREEZE: the last frame held for 24 frames with literally nothing moving, no drift, no push, no grain animation. Absence of motion is the rest beat a silent film uses in place of the pause before the logo.
shots.screenTreatment: Full bleed, crop tight enough that 'pi finished' is unambiguously readable at 1920x1080.
shots.typeTreatment: None. Five instances of the word 'finished' are the type, and they are the product's.
shots.feature: Inbox — know the moment it is done

shots.what: f1092-1200. Ink. The muxr display-matrix wordmark assembles one cell column at a time, f1104-1126. From f1126 to f1160 one mono line types out centre-aligned so it grows outward from the middle, with a solid block cursor leading the edge: 'Leave the desk. Not the work.' The cursor stays lit and blinks on Math.floor(frame/12)%2. f1168: two micro lines fade in dim — 'npm install -g --ignore-scripts @trymuxr/cli' and 'trymuxr.com'. Held dead still f1186-1192. 8 frames to black.
shots.camera: None. Absolutely static for the full 108 frames.
shots.screenTreatment: None. No product, no screenshot, no device. Nobody ends on a product screenshot.
shots.typeTreatment: The wordmark, one typed mono line, two micro lines. Total. The block cursor is the film's signature because terminal typography is native to this product rather than borrowed.
shots.transitionIn: Fade through black, 15 frames, starting from the frozen inbox frame. The only dissolve in the entire film.

technique.name: The device is bolted to the frame; only light and pixels move
technique.why: Removes the single biggest cheap tell in Remotion 3D work — the tumbling, spinning, floating mockup phone. Apple's own partner guideline forbids animating, flipping or spinning the product, and their films obey it: roughly 40% of shots are fully locked off.
technique.how: Shot 2 only. <ThreeCanvas width height linear> with the group's rotation/position/scale as constants, not interpolations. Body: extrudeGeometry over a THREE.Shape rounded rect (bevelEnabled true, bevelSize 0, bevelThickness 0) in meshPhysicalMaterial{color:'#0d0d0f',metalness:0.9,roughness:0.28,clearcoat:1,clearcoatRoughness:0.1,envMapIntensity:1.2}. Screen: a SEPARATE shapeGeometry rounded-rect plane sitting proud of the body with meshBasicMaterial toneMapped={false} — that flag is what stops the UI going muddy. ContactShadows frames={1} opacity={0.55} blur={2.6} far={4}, plus a second wide ambient shadow div at 6% opacity behind the canvas. Absolutely no drei <Float>, <CameraShake>, <Sparkles>, <Stars>, <Trail>, <AccumulativeShadows>, or MeshTransmissionMaterial temporalDistortion — all of them run useFrame internally and will vibrate between renders.

technique.name: Studio lighting with no HDRI and no 3D artist
technique.why: The template-three default (ambientLight + pointLight + meshPhongMaterial) is the 2011-CGI look: flat, one hard specular dot, no reflections. Reflections are what read as expensive, and the Apple 45° glass sweep is what makes a render look photographed.
technique.how: <Environment resolution={256} frames={1}> containing three drei <Lightformer> planes and no external file: a long strip at 45° across the upper right (the key, the thing that produces the sweep), a broad soft fill at frame left, and a thin rim behind. frames={1} bakes the cube render target once so it is deterministic. The sweep itself comes from interpolating the key Lightformer's position.x off useCurrentFrame() between f186 and f240 — the light travels, the device does not. envMapIntensity carries the whole look; you need no scene lights at all.

technique.name: Real mp4 as the 3D screen texture, via CanvasTexture
technique.why: Fake or rebuilt UI reads as fake inside four frames, and Apple's own rule on the M1 Max film was that anything on screen had to actually be on the screen. useVideoTexture and useOffthreadVideoTexture are both deprecated.
technique.how: const [gfx] = useState(() => { const canvas = new OffscreenCanvas(1080,2400); const context = canvas.getContext('2d'); return {canvas, context, texture: new CanvasTexture(canvas)}; }). Render <Video src={staticFile('shots/dark/herd.mp4')} muted headless onVideoFrame={cb}> from @remotion/media inside the canvas tree; in cb do gfx.context.drawImage(frame,0,0,1080,2400); gfx.texture.needsUpdate = true; then advance(performance.now()) when useRemotionEnvironment().isRendering, else invalidate(). advance() not invalidate() during render is mandatory — invalidate only queues and the screenshot captures the previous texture.

technique.name: Grade the real captures instead of decorating around them
technique.why: This is most of the gap and it needs no 3D at all. The previous six versions were built as if Remotion were still a div-and-interpolate library; @remotion/effects is a real GPU compositing stack and closes most of the distance to an After Effects grade in one pass.
technique.how: npm i @remotion/effects@4.0.514 — it is NOT currently in tools/demo/package.json. Then per shot, on the

technique.name: Rack focus and falling light without a 3D camera
technique.why: Per-layer defocus across one surface is the measured difference between Linear's films and a slide — a perspective-warped bitmap is uniformly sharp or uniformly soft, and the eye classifies the uniform one as a picture of a screen.
technique.how: radialProgressiveBlur({center, width, height, start, startBlur:0, endBlur:14}) with center interpolated onto the lifted approve row in shot 7 — that is the rack. linearProgressiveBlur({start:[0,0.15], end:[0,1], startBlur:0, endBlur:40}) with endBlur ramped from useCurrentFrame() is the laptop closing in shot 1. Both are deterministic pure functions of props; neither needs R3F, postprocessing, or a depth pass.

technique.name: Cut on the frame an on-screen motion completes, on a 6-frame grid
technique.why: There is no music, so the completion of a UI movement IS the downbeat. And keeping every cut interval a whole multiple of 6 frames lets the eye build a metronome the ear cannot.
technique.how: All thirteen shot lengths are multiples of 6f (0.2s): 156, 114, 78, 96, 78, 108, 60, 78, 78, 66, 96, 84, 108. lib/moments.json already scores every frame of every capture for how much changed and names the best window at 1.5/2/2.5/3/3.5/4s — pick the window from that data, then nudge the out-point to the nearest 6f boundary that lands on a completed motion.

technique.name: Content-derived staggered reveals, from the captures themselves
technique.why: Rebuilding UI as layers is a person-week. Scanning the capture for its own row boundaries gives per-element reveals from real footage for about forty lines of code — the highest craft-per-line move available here.
technique.how: capture/fragments.mjs already finds the nav-chip boundaries by scanning a pixel row for its ground value rather than hard-coding them. Run the identical scan down the vertical axis of raw/dark/plugins.png and raw/dark/inbox.png to emit per-row [y,h] rects, write them beside the fragments, and use them as per-row masks. Each row then enters on opacity + 14px translateY + blur(12px to 0) simultaneously, 4-5f stagger. Three properties minimum — a plain fadeIn is not an animation, and 2f of stagger reads as simultaneous.

technique.name: The lift punches a hole in the plane it came from
technique.why: This is the step everyone skips and the one that matters. Lift an element and leave the original underneath and it reads as a sticker on a screenshot; darken and blur the vacated rect and the element genuinely came out of somewhere.
technique.how: Shot 7. The approve row crops to its own absolutely-positioned layer, translateZ-equivalent 90px toward camera on spring({frame,fps,config:{damping:200,mass:3}}), with dropShadow({radius:18,offsetX:0,offsetY:14,opacity:0.28}) — a contact shadow whose offset is no larger than the lift distance, not a generic drop shadow. Simultaneously the source rect on the parent gets brightness(0.82) and blur(6px) via a clip-path'd overlay div at the same coordinates.

technique.name: Press states go darker and in, never lighter and up
technique.why: The most-repeated amateur tell in the SaaS-film literature is scaling a button UP and brightening it on press. Real touch targets recess.
technique.how: scale 0.97, brightness 0.88, 90ms in / 140ms out — 3 frames in, 5 frames out at 30fps, both on Easing.bezier(0.42,0,0.58,1). Applied on the send arrow and the ^C key in shot 3 and the approve row in shot 7. No cursor, no finger, no tap dot anywhere in the film: the app's own press state, exaggerated, is the interaction language. Tap dots are tutorial grammar, not marketing grammar.

technique.name: One camera move per shot, at least 25%, then locked — and never while the content moves
technique.why: A 3-8% drift on every shot is the Ken Burns tell. A move means something only when some shots do not have one. Six of thirteen shots here are fully locked; two carry only a sub-2% breathing push; three carry a real move.
technique.how: Every scale animation goes through interpolate(frame, [a,b], [s0,s1], {easing: Easing.bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), output:'perceptual-scale', extrapolateLeft:'clamp', extrapolateRight:'clamp'}). output:'perceptual-scale' compensates for scale being perceptually non-linear and almost nobody uses it. One axis per move. The shot-6 push lands ON the gutter at the frame the approve is about to happen; the shot-11 pull-back is 3.9x and decelerates hard into its final 18 locked frames.

technique.name: Velocity-derived motion blur instead of CameraMotionBlur
technique.why: <CameraMotionBlur samples={10}> renders the subtree ten times and the docs warn it is destructive to colour; wrapping an R3F canvas in it multiplies GPU cost by ten. A blur keyed to your own velocity gets 80% of the read for nothing.
technique.how: Compute the scale/position delta between frame and frame-1 from the same interpolate call, then blur = Math.abs(delta) * k, applied as blur() from @remotion/effects, plus chromaticAberration({amount:2}) at peak velocity only. 2-4px of fringe, never 8. Peaks ~5px around f930 in the pull-back and ~4px mid-push in shot 6.

technique.name: Two grounds, cut against each other, never dissolved
technique.why: The brief requires both light and dark. Alternating them randomly is 'inconsistent'; assigning one act to paper and cutting hard into it is a decision. And keeping the type block in the identical grid position across the flip is what tells the viewer it was intentional.
technique.how: ground.ink '#0a0a0c' and ground.paper '#f2f1ed' already exist in reel/src/design.ts. Shots 6 and 7 (the review act) run on paper with light/changes.mp4; everything else runs on ink with the dark captures. Both flips are hard cuts with the screen filling frame on both sides, so only the ground changes. Mean frame luma stays in the 6-14% band for every ink shot — Linear's measured discipline, and the film never fades to #000 except the final 8 frames.

technique.name: The colour budget, spent on the app's own status hues at dot size
technique.why: The client hates green dominating a frame, and there is no brand colour. The product's own rule (components/ui.tsx) is that status hues go on text, dots and small glyphs, never on a fill wider than a number.
technique.how: Total saturated pixels in the film: one 10px #0A84FF working dot in shots 1 and 2; the diff gutter's native red/green line marks at line height in shot 6; one 10px #30D158 done dot in shot 10; five 10px #30D158 finished dots in shot 12. Nothing else. No gradient, no tint pass, no accent fill, no purple-on-dark. The end card has zero colour.

technique.name: The freeze, and the typed line with a block cursor
technique.why: Silence before the logo is what a soundtrack does; 24 frames where nothing at all moves is the silent equivalent, and it is the reason the end card lands rather than arrives. The typed mono line with a solid block cursor is Linear's exact ending — and for a terminal product it is native typography, not borrowed.
technique.how: Hold shot 12's final frame for 24f with every interpolate clamped and the grain seed fixed so even the noise stops. Then a 15f fade through black. On the card, characters = Math.floor(interpolate(frame,[1126,1160],[0,LINE.length])) rendered centre-aligned so the line grows outward from the middle; the cursor is a filled block glyph whose visibility is Math.floor(frame/12)%2 — frame-derived, never Date.now(), never requestAnimationFrame.

risks: PERSONAL DATA LEAK, blocking: raw/dark/connection.mp4 and raw/light/connection.mp4 print the owner's real tailnet host, 'wss://extreme.tail0de54.ts.net'. capture/mask.mjs masks only the PNG, not the video. @remotion/effects is not installed — it is absent from tools/demo/package.json even though @remotion/media, /three, /transitions, /paths and /shapes at 4.0.514 all are. Every grade, vignette, glow, progressive blur and chromatic aberration in this treatment depends on it. npm i @remotion/effects@4.0.514 before shot one.

Resolution budget. Captures are 1080x2400; at full frame height in 1920x1080 that is ~45% scale, so there is 2.2x of punch-in before you interpolate. Shot 11 opens at 2.4x and shot 3 is a tight crop of a 1080-wide source. Mitigate by starting shot 11's first 12 frames on the sharp raw/dark/herd.png still, or recapture with adb shell wm size 1440x3120 && wm density 560 first, which raises the ceiling on every shot at the cost of one line.

The voice capture is a small particle orb on near-black: lib/moments.json reports dark/voice with alive 0.001 across a 101.9s recording, because YAVG frame-differencing on a mostly-black frame reads the real motion as noise. Any automatic window-finder will pick the wrong three seconds. Hand-set the voice in-point, and crop to the frag/orb rect [150,380,780,780] — the untouched screen is roughly 70% empty black and will read as a dead frame at full bleed.

Determinism in the R3F shot. @remotion/three calls advance(performance.now()) once per Remotion frame, so useFrame, state.clock and anything with an internal time uniform map render jitter onto the transform and differ between two renders of the same composition. Both <Environment> and <ContactShadows> must carry frames={1}, any <Sequence> inside <ThreeCanvas> must carry layout="none", and shot 2 should be rendered twice and byte-diffed before anything else is built on top of it.

Four of the eight capabilities carry no caption at all and rest entirely on the product's own on-screen text being legible at 1920x1080 — the ctrl/shift/esc/^C key row, '269.4M / $177', 'Local plugin · UI only', '16 agents', 'pi finished'. If any crop is set too wide to read that text, the claim silently vanishes and the shot degrades to texture. Check every crop at 100% before locking, and treat '16 agents' in shot 11 as the single most load-bearing string in the film.
storeFrames: Stop designing the store frames as a separate deliverable. Every one of the eight becomes the poster frame of the film shot it corresponds to — same capture, same crop, same ground, same grid position, same kicker numbering, same two type registers — so the carousel reads as eight stills pulled out of the film rather than a parallel design that happens to share a font. That also means frames/render.mjs stops being a layout engine and becomes a still renderer pointed at the same beat definitions the film uses, which removes the drift that made the last set feel like a different product. Order follows the film's spine, not the app's nav menu: (1) the film's literal opening frame — one LIVE pane card at macro on ink, blue working dot, no type at all, because a carousel opening on a headline is a slide and this one opens on evidence; (2) the device establish, whole handset straight-on on ink, 'The same pane. In your pocket.' in display type beside it in the negative space, never over it; (3) terminal keys and composer full bleed on ink, ctrl/shift/esc/tab/^C legible, no type — the key caps are the caption; (4) the voice orb macro on ink with 'Say it. Don't type it.' left; (5) the diff on paper — the one light frame in the set, dual gutter and per-file tab rail, 'Read it before you approve.'; (6) the spend numbers on ink, 269.4M / $177 / 1.7B / $1461 large enough to read at Play thumbnail size, one mono micro line 'READ FROM YOUR OWN LOGS'; (7) plugins rows plus the authoring CLI panel split at 62/38 on ink, 'NATIVE UI. NO WEBVIEWS.' in mono micro, with '$ muxr plugin create field-notes' visible in the panel; (8) the pull-back's wide — the Spaces list with 'pockit /home/umer/pockit — 16 agents' legible in the product's own type, and zero marketing type on the frame. Store frame 8 is the film's payoff frame and it should be the last thing a browsing user sees. Three constraints carried over from the film: the connection screen does not get a store frame at all until the relay host is masked in both media; the green budget stays at dot size, which for the whole carousel means the status dots in frames 1 and 8 and the diff's + marks in frame 5; and every frame must survive being the only one someone looks at, which is the real test frames/render.mjs should be run against.
